propositions: Jira mutations are currently decided and executed across multiple layers (differ, apply wrapper, ACLI/REST, DC SDK, handlers, batch orchestration) with fragmented retry ownership and no stable per-ticket or batch-scoped failure classification.

No existing mechanism bounds physical retry attempts (calls), cumulative latency, or endpoint-failure-rate breaker; only a per-pass blast-radius guard exists but does not prevent exhausted endpoint failures.

A provider-neutral coordinator must model each logical postcondition within three physical invocations and 15 seconds total sleep, honor provider rate-limit lower bounds, and defer long waits instead of retrying early.

The coordinator must classify outcomes (auto-healed, retryable, permanent, commit-unknown, ticket-local, endpoint, tenant, provider, global) with exact per-ticket and per-pass tallies and activate a three-consecutive scoped endpoint-failure fuse independent of the retained blast-radius guard.

Create operations must enforce label-first containment using `rebar-id:<local_id>`, optional property enrichment, and known-key safety-abort to prevent duplicates after timeout or persistence failure.

Shadow planning must produce deterministic immutable per-ticket plans (mutations, lifecycle intents, dependencies, diagnostics, dispositions) from one observation without remote or local writes, enabling cutover by operation family without dual-writes.
